# Bounded scheduler operational limits

The opt-in workflows run at most two concurrent Lean builds (`-j 1` each); the command-line `--workers` option can set another positive limit. This bounds build-process concurrency, not total processes, physical memory, or aggregate job memory. In the 4.33 workflow the 24 GiB virtual-address limit is per process, not shared: two Lean processes may each approach it, alongside Lake, Python, caches, and other job processes. The other workflow does not set this limit. Runner capacity and peak combined memory have not been established; do not treat the experimental bounded mode as resource-safe without measuring it on the intended runner. The default remains serial.

The scheduler polls running children before each dispatch batch and stops dispatching once a failure is observed. A process can fail after its poll and before another process starts, including within a dispatch batch; strict observation before every new dispatch cannot be guaranteed by polling. Dependency barriers and result checks are unchanged.

During the bounded build, SIGTERM and SIGINT request cancellation. The scheduler signals tracked process groups with SIGTERM, gives them a short opportunity to reap children, escalates to SIGKILL, and waits for direct children. This covers descendants that remain in their build's process group; descendants that create a new session or process group escape it. The scheduler cannot reap non-child descendants unless separately adopted by the OS, and cannot guarantee cleanup after SIGKILL, a crash, host shutdown, or signals delivered only to an outer wrapper. Cleanup of orphaned zombies depends on their reaper. The serial build and subsequent axiom query use separate subprocess paths and do not have this bounded-scheduler cancellation guarantee. Runner-level cancellation and aggregate resource containment remain unverified.
